title: Calculating the Treadwear Adjustment Credit — Tire Sets & Treadwear Limited Warranty
content:
**The treadwear adjustment credit for one worn wheel position of a Tire Sets & Treadwear Limited Warranty set is the price paid per tire times the adjustment's credit percentage divided by 100, rounded half up to the cent.** Installation charges, fees and tax never enter it.

The quantities, in the order they are worked out:

1. **Miles run** — the odometer of the set's latest tread inspection, which is the inspection the adjustment rests on, less the set's install odometer.
2. **Covered-mileage percentage** — 100.
3. **Covered miles** — the line's warranted miles times the covered-mileage percentage divided by 100, rounded down to a whole mile.
4. **Unreceived share** — the covered miles less the miles run, times 100, divided by the covered miles; it is 0 when the miles run are at or above the covered miles.
5. **Credit percentage** — the unreceived share rounded down to a whole percent; the credit is 0.00 when that whole percent is below the line's minimum adjustment percentage.
6. **Price paid per tire** — the price per tire on the set's own ticket. The percentage is taken of the price paid per tire on the set's own ticket for every tire line, and the store's selling price on the adjustment date does not enter it.

The credit percentage is rounded down to a whole percent before the minimum-percentage test; no other intermediate figure is rounded, and the credit is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

### Worked figures (hypothetical set; figures invented for illustration)
| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Line's warranted miles | 50,000 |
| Latest inspection odometer less install odometer | 37,000 miles run |
| Covered miles | 50,000 |
| Unreceived share | 13,000 times 100 divided by 50,000: 26 |
| Credit percentage | 26%, above a 10% minimum |
| Price per tire on the ticket | $150.00 |
| Credit | $39.00 |

With 46,000 miles run on the same hypothetical set, the unreceived share is 8 and, against a 10% minimum, the credit is 0.00.
